method: Counts are derived from the loop bounds the tests actually use, not written down beside them, so a bound that changes changes this artifact. Every case is compared against C's strtod bit for bit, including the number of bytes consumed.
test_names: fixed lexemes match libc strtod exactly
long digit strings match libc strtod
exponent sweep across the whole double range
powers of two and their neighbours
hex floats match libc strtod, including past 53 bits of mantissa
randomised hex floats match libc strtod
nan payloads that overflow 64 bits are implementation-defined
json_get_number on a string token follows strtod prefix rules
limitation: This records coverage of the *conversion*, compared against the platform's strtod. Agreement with libc is compatibility; correctness under IEEE-754 is a separate question, answered for the hex-float grammar by scripts/hexfloat_oracle.py against an exact-integer reference.
